verdicts.verify_by: run gno test -v -run TestB1LetterlikeMathLetters with the same artifact: validText("ℤℴℴℳ") and validText("ℂℍℕ") should be false; both are observed true. The U+1D400 control is refused
verdicts.tldr: Titles written entirely in the double-struck, script and fraktur letters of Letterlike Symbols (U+2102-214F) pass validText and keep a key distinct from the Latin word they draw, although the code says mathematical alphanumerics are refused
verdicts.details: isMimic refuses only U+1D400-1D7FF, and the letters that block leaves as holes live in Letterlike Symbols (ℂ ℍ ℕ ℙ ℚ ℝ ℤ, ℬ ℰ ℱ ℋ ℐ ℒ ℳ ℛ ℯ ℊ ℴ, ℭ ℌ ℑ ℜ ℨ). They are script Common, so the Latin branch never runs; IsLetter sets foreign, and with no Latin letter in the title `alnum && (!latin || !foreign)` accepts it. titleKey does not fold them because ToLower leaves them unchanged and foldRune has no case for them, so "ℤℴℴℳ" gets a different key from "Zoom" and both get listed. The reach is narrow: mixing one of these letters with ASCII is refused by the Latin/foreign rule and mixing with U+1D400 is refused by isMimic, so only words spelled from about 25 letters get through. It still contradicts the isMimic comment and T6, and the realm is v0 and frozen once deployed. Fix: add the Letterlike letter range to isMimic, e.g. `r >= 0x2102 && r <= 0x214F && unicode.IsLetter(r)`, keeping 0x212A/0x212B, which are already Latin and refused by commonLatin.
verdicts.evidence: Head, scratch worktree, finder's artifact copied as b1_claims_fold_test.gno: gno test -v -run TestB1LetterlikeMathLetters . -> "ℤℴℴℳ" accepted though T6 says mathematical alphanumerics are refused / "ℂℍℕ" accepted though T6 says mathematical alphanumerics are refused / --- FAIL; no 'control failed' line, so U+1D400 is refused. Read validate.gno:182-186: `return unicode.Is(unicode.Me, r) || r >= 0xFF01 && r <= 0xFF5E || r >= 0x1D400 && r <= 0x1D7FF`. Base: r/gnoland/store does not exist at the merge base (ls: No such file or directory), so the diff introduces this.

verdicts.verify_by: filetest with names enabled: register alice, deploy r/alice/swap with Register in init, UpdateName to alice2, try RegisterUser('alice') from a second address, then Claim from it; read Render("api/v1/...") for the slug's title and kind. If the name cannot be retaken, band drops to Suggestion (owner loses edit rights)
verdicts.tldr: No second address can ever hold a renamed or deleted user's old name, so no one else gets Claim authority over that user's deployed app's listing; what remains is that the renamed owner loses Claim on r/alice/*, which is r/sys/names policy
verdicts.details: Claim authorises through names.IsAuthorizedAddressForNamespace, which via resolveCurrentName grants only the current holder of a name. r/sys/users never removes a name: it has no nameStore.Remove, delete() only sets u.deleted = true, and registerUser refuses any name already in nameStore with ErrNameTaken, the GovDAO ProposeRegisterUser path included. So the takeover step in the scenario cannot happen. The leftover is the finder's own fallback: after renaming, alice2 can no longer Claim to edit r/alice/swap's listing, but the realm can still update it through its own Register. That follows from r/sys/names' documented rename policy, not from a store defect. Fix: none needed in the store; at most, note in Claim's doc that a rename gives up Claim over the old namespace's listings.
verdicts.evidence: Head, judge test copied into r/sys/users: gno test -v -run TestJudge30 . -> --- PASS: TestJudge30RenamedNameNotRetakable (register alice, UpdateName alice2, ResolveName("alice") isCurrent=false, RegisterUser("alice", bob) errors ErrNameTaken) / --- PASS: TestJudge30DeletedNameNotRetakable (same after Delete). Read r/sys/users/store.gno:93-95 and grep: no nameStore.Remove anywhere in r/sys/users. Base: r/gnoland/store is absent at the merge base.
verdicts.refuted_by: r/sys/users/store.gno:93 if nameStore.Has(name) { return ErrNameTaken } (nameStore is never pruned: no nameStore.Remove in r/sys/users)
